Windows GPU UNLOCK

 English 한국어

Contributor tooling: entry-point inventory and cleanup proposal.

Experimental UEFI GPU unlock and direct Windows handoff, expanded through
community contributions.

 
 
 

 Start here

 Want to find out about your PC or help report compatibility? Start with a Windows-only check. You do not need to attempt an unlock.

 Your goal What to do 
 :--- :--- 
 I'm new. What information should I report? Beginner guide: check your PC and share results 
 I already have capture files from my PC Check those files offline 
 I want to know which setups have worked Reported setups and their limits 
 I'm ready to investigate an unlock Check the exact configuration and boot route first 

 Quick check · No reboot

This prints hardware/driver information; it does not unlock, change settings or upload anything. not-assessed and can unlock: false are normal. Remove personal details from the output, then paste the reviewed text into a compatibility report. Do not attach firmware or raw dumps.

 [!TIP]
 No Python or terminal experience? The step-by-step guide explains how to start, what the result means and what to share. You can also enter hardware details manually; no EFI test is required to report findings.

 Community

 GPU support

 Success reports apply to specific cards and systems, not every card of the same
GPU model. Check the linked motherboard, BIOS and card requirements before building.

The compatibility guide lists exact build profiles and
distinguishes maintainer tests from contributor reports. Results concern their
recorded builds; later main-branch hardening has host/build checks, not a new
physical boot or recovery test .

The latest tagged release, v0.3.1, is a source-only pre-release . This source
tree has changes beyond that tag, including the USB route and X870 profile; those
are not a newly published release. Build locally with your own partition GUIDs.
Firmware assets and private, partition-specific EFI binaries are not bundled.

All reported working setups and profile coverage · Complete issue audit.

 Path Display and input Instructions 
 --- --- --- 
 Internal headless B650M/3090 FE or B660M/3070 Ti / 3090 Ti profile; monitors on RTX; display temporarily removed; no T/U/Enter Internal headless guide 
 Headless USB Reported RTX 3060 / 3090 Ti configurations; profile-specific wrapper and child on a FAT32 USB stick Headless USB guide 
 Internal AMD-display manual / Auto Original B650M profile, motherboard/iGPU display preserved; manual variant requires U Existing internal guide 
 Legacy USB manual Original AMD/iGPU display profile; U once, then Boot Override to Windows without reset Legacy USB guide 

For the original B650M machine with one motherboard display and two RTX displays,
see the opt-in AMD-retained experiment.
One manual boot succeeded on its recorded private build; automatic boot and the
integrated revision still require their own physical verification.

X870, B660-PLUS and H610M are not wired into Configure.ps1 or Headless.ps1 ; use the USB guide.
USB packages can also be built for the first two profiles, but their recorded
internal boots do not validate those USB routes. The legacy USB EFI retains its
AMD display requirement. BIOS priority USB → Windows alone does not implement
direct handoff.

install.title: Internal headless quick start
install.html:
Advanced · Exact-profile internal headless setup

This example is for the default B650M / RTX 3090 FE profile. For B660M, select -HardwareProfile b660m-3070ti in both configuration and build as described in compatibility. X870 uses the separate USB route.

Read the full guide and recovery procedure before changing boot settings. Use the exact supported hardware, Secure Boot disabled, a fully decrypted Windows C: with BitLocker protection off, and a connected keyboard. The tools do not disable encryption.

Preserve the existing Windows ESP and recovery partition. Prepare a separate GPT FAT32 EFI System Partition of at least 1 GiB, with a letter such as U:. Tools do not create, shrink, delete or format partitions. An ordinary FAT32 data partition alone is not the required ESP.

You need Python 3.9+, clang/lld-link 20.1.8, the pinned repository dependencies and five locally obtained firmware assets. Host integration tests additionally need MSVC/Windows SDK and private fixtures.

From an administrator PowerShell in the repository root:

# Replace the GUID and tool paths with your own values.
.\internal-boot\Configure.ps1 -UnlockDriveLetter U `
  -WindowsEspGuid 'YOUR-WINDOWS-ESP-GUID'
.\research\headless\build-unlock.ps1 `
  -Clang 'C:\TOOLS\LLVM20\bin\clang.exe' `
  -LldLink 'C:\TOOLS\LLVM20\bin\lld-link.exe'

# Stage and append a separate F8 test entry; retain existing boot priority.
.\internal-boot\Headless.ps1 -Assets '.\assets' -Register

Without an action switch, Headless.ps1 -Assets '.\assets' only stages files. Configuration and build do not register a boot entry.

  1. Save work and fully power off. On the tested ASUS firmware, select F8 → GPU Headless UNLOCK - EXPERIMENTAL.

  2. Wait without T, U or Enter. Initial Esc within five seconds skips release and unlock and boots Windows directly.

  3. The screen becomes black while the RTX GOP is removed. The child attempts once and the wrapper starts Windows directly. Do not reset between unlock and Windows. Confirm display recovery and measure.

  4. Only after that F8 test succeeds, enable default automatic boot:

    .\internal-boot\Headless.ps1 -EnableAutomatic -ConfirmedSuccess

That explicit action places headless first and Windows Boot Manager second and disables Windows Fast Startup. Test registration alone does not. Publishing this release does not change the research PC's current default boot selection.

The two Esc windows differ: initial wrapper Esc boots Windows without release; the later three-second child Esc window is after release and cancels into a stop. It does not restore the display or continue to Windows. On failure or if Windows does not return, fully power off and choose F8 → Windows Boot Manager.

.\internal-boot\Headless.ps1 -RestoreWindowsFirst

Windows-first recovery is independent of experimental EFI/build artifacts and still works without saved state. Restoring the prior Fast Startup setting needs that state; retain it and backups. Recovery details.
